data.title: Islamic Affairs Ministry Concludes Fourth Scholarly Course in Sri Lanka
data.content:
Colombo, November 21, 2026, SPA -- The Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Dawah and Guidance, represented by the Religious Attaché’s Office at the Kingdom’s Embassy in New Delhi, has concluded its fourth foundational scholarly course in Colombo, Sri Lanka. The initiative was held in cooperation with relevant religious authorities and under the supervision of the Kingdom’s Embassy in Sri Lanka, with more than 550 participants, including imams, preachers, religious scholars, academics, and male and female students of Islamic knowledge.
    The course is part of the ministry’s ongoing efforts to disseminate Islamic knowledge, establish the correct creed, promote moderation and balance, and train personnel in religious outreach.
    Participants praised the initiative and commended the Kingdom’s efforts, under the leadership of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, in serving Islam and Muslims. They also stressed the importance of continuing these programs and expanding them to various regions of Sri Lanka.
    -- SPA
